nodes.task: Independently extract and recompute all operations metrics from input/operations.csv and persist metrics.json. Steps: (1) list the working directory and read input/operations.csv in full, capturing its header and every data row; (2) record a hash-independent confirmation that the file is read-only in this workflow — do not modify, rewrite, reformat, normalize, or append to it in any way; (3) from the raw per-row integer fields compute, for the overall dataset and each of the three teams Atlas, Birch and Cedar: work_orders (sum of work orders), completed_orders (sum of completed), defects (sum of defects), planned_minutes (sum of planned minutes), actual_minutes (sum of actual minutes), completion_percent = completed_orders / work_orders * 100 rounded half-up to exactly 2 decimal places, minutes_per_completed_order = actual_minutes / completed_orders rounded half-up to exactly 2 decimal places, schedule_variance_minutes = actual_minutes - planned_minutes as an integer; (4) verify row_count equals the literal number of data rows actually read, and verify that each totals integer field equals the sum of the corresponding Atlas+Birch+Cedar values, adjusting only if the raw data proves otherwise and reporting any discrepancy explicitly rather than silently forcing numbers; (5) write metrics.json with root keys in the exact order row_count, totals, teams; totals and each team object keys in the exact order work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes, completion_percent, minutes_per_completed_order, schedule_variance_minutes; teams keys in the exact order Atlas, Birch, Cedar; no additional or nested fields anywhere. All integer metrics must serialize as JSON numbers (no strings, no trailing .0); completion_percent and minutes_per_completed_order must serialize with exactly two decimal places even when the second decimal is a zero (e.g. 83.33, 71.15), so use a fixed 2-decimal numeric rendering rather than float repr. Expected reference shape (must be confirmed against the real CSV, not copied blindly): row_count 18, totals work_orders 233, completed_orders 217, defects 18, planned_minutes 14985, actual_minutes 15440, completion_percent 93.13, minutes_per_completed_order 71.15, schedule_variance_minutes 455; Atlas 95/89/7/5700/5780/93.68/64.94/80; Birch 75/71/3/4875/4910/94.67/69.15/35; Cedar 63/57/8/4410/4750/90.48/83.33/340. If your recomputation disagrees with any of these reference values, do not overwrite your computed value to match — report the discrepancy in your task output and flag it for the Head.

After metrics.json exists, synthesize operations-brief.md for management. Steps: (1) read the persisted metrics.json and independently re-read input/operations.csv to confirm the figures you cite trace to real rows; (2) write a concise, decision-oriented executive recommendation grounded strictly in this six-week three-team dataset — for example, note that Cedar carries the widest schedule variance and highest minutes per completed order while having the lowest completion percent, so remediation should target Cedar, with Atlas's positive variance and defect count as a secondary reliability concern; keep the recommendation proportionate and avoid claims the data cannot support; (3) state exact overall findings: work orders, completed orders, defects, completion percent, minutes per completed order, planned and actual minutes, schedule variance; (4) state exact per-team findings for Atlas, Birch and Cedar covering completion percent, completed vs work orders, defects, and schedule variance in minutes, using the same figures and precision as metrics.json (two decimals for percent and minutes per order, plain integers for counts and minutes), with no arithmetic divergence from metrics.json; (5) include a Method section that names input/operations.csv as the sole source and states exactly these three formulas: completion percent = completed orders / work orders × 100; minutes per completed order = actual minutes / completed orders; schedule variance = actual minutes − planned minutes; also note that aggregates are summed from raw rows and rounded to two decimals only at presentation time, and that no units were converted and no records were invented; (6) keep the document short and readable — an executive recommendation, an overall findings block, a per-team findings block, and the Method section — with no invented data, no external benchmarks, no forecasts beyond the supplied dataset, and no mention of tooling internals.
